newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech ruling coalition delays energy price debate.
newsitem.headline: Czech ruling coalition delays energy price debate.

text.p: The Czech ruling coalition delayed on Thursday a decision on raising controlled prices on energy and heating, possibly for weeks, deputy premier Josef Lux told a news conference.

He said that the cabinet would discuss a proposal to raise value added tax on electricity and gas to 22 percent from five percent next Wednesday, and then the coalition leaders would discuss a plan to raise utility prices themselves the following week.

The change in the value added tax must must gain final approval in the parliament as a change in the overall tax code, before being implemented. The plan under consideration, submitted by the finance ministry, is for the tax change to take effect on July 1 this year.
Lux said leaders would meet within two weeks to discuss the overall hikes in electricity, gas, and heating prices.
Plans within the coalition vary from minor price hikes to a radical restructuring of utility prices.
The ruling coalition has a broad agreement that changes need to be made to balance the cross-subsidising of household energy costs which heavily burden industry.
The statement followed a meeting of leaders of the three parties which make up the centre-right coalition government.
The parties agreed to make a joint decision on housing and energy deregulation policy in the coalition agreement which formed the government following 1996 general elections.
Earlier the coalition agreed to fully deregulate almost all state-controlled rents on housing by 2000.
